incidents.summary: Throughout late July 2026, the wildfire incident in southern France's Pyrénées-Orientales area escalated dramatically amid a broader crisis of wildfires across southwestern France and Spain. Massive fires forced over 360,000 people to evacuate, with the blaze near Bordeaux prompting 84,000 to return home on July 30 as cooler weather arrived, while a separate fast-moving fire in the Var department flared on July 22. Romania extended its firefighting mission by two weeks, and French firefighters created tree-cutting firebreaks as they described the system at breaking point, with President Macron calling the situation France's biggest challenge since WWII.

incidents.summary:
New reports indicate over 250,000 people have now been evacuated across France and Spain, with at least one death confirmed in Spain. High winds gusting up to 60 kph are complicating firefighting efforts, and the Tour de France has shortened its final stage due to the emergency.
As of July 25-26, the number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 300,000, with exhausted firefighters battling blazes fueled by high winds. At least one death has been confirmed in Spain, and the Tour de France final stage has been shortened to free up security personnel for firefighting efforts.
A new wildfire broke out in Castellon, Valencia, forcing 15,000 evacuations. As of July 26, France has evacuated about 220,000 people and Spain over 75,000 (with 30,000 ordered to shelter in place), while Bordeaux considered a total evacuation as fires advanced to within 15 kilometers of the city. French President Macron called a crisis cabinet meeting for Monday to address the escalating situation.

It is considered one of Spain's deadliest wildfires on record.

logs.summary:
A massive wildfire in central Spain has burned over 32,000 hectares (79,000 acres), becoming one of the country's largest on record, forcing thousands to evacuate. The Spanish government declared a national emergency on July 24 as the blaze continued to rage. Three firefighters died in associated wildfires across Europe, with two in France and one in Italy, while Spain's annual wildfire average was crossed before August.
Spain declared its first-ever national emergency as wildfires near Madrid and Avila forced 20,000 evacuations, while in southwestern France over 60,000 people, including tourists, were evacuated from the Cap Ferret peninsula by boat. Both countries requested assistance from the European Union as the fires, fueled by a marine heatwave and extreme temperatures, burned over 100 square kilometers in France.
The total number of evacuees from wildfires in Spain and France has risen to over 90,000, with 40,000 people ordered to evacuate or shelter in the Madrid region alone. A major wildfire in southern France near Cap Ferret is now reported to be under control, though blazes continue to rage in central Spain. Authorities are deploying novel firefighting methods, including using donkeys to graze flammable vegetation.

logs.summary:
By July 24-25, wildfires in southwestern France and central Spain forced over 200,000 people to evacuate, with France reporting 141,000 evacuees from the Gironde and Landes departments and Spain evacuating 60,000. French President Emmanuel Macron ordered military mobilization as a blaze approached the city of Bordeaux, while Spain's national emergency declaration covered the Madrid region and Avila province. Dozens of firefighters were injured but no deaths were reported.
On July 25, 2026, about 20,000 people were evacuated from towns along the French Atlantic coast as a wildfire spread, while around 197,000 evacuations were ordered in the Gironde and Landes regions. France prepared an A400M aircraft to drop retardant on the Gironde wildfire near Bordeaux, and evacuations also occurred near Madrid in Spain as blazes continued.
By July 25, the total number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 267,000, with France evacuating suburbs of Bordeaux as a massive wildfire shifts toward the city. France deployed a specially adapted A400M cargo aircraft to dump flame retardants on the blaze, and French President Macron stated the country "will rebuild" after the fires. Officials described the Madrid wildfire as the "worst fire in the history of the region" and the final stage of the Tour de France was shortened due to the fires.

logs.summary:
New reports indicate over 250,000 people have now been evacuated across France and Spain, with at least one death confirmed in Spain. High winds gusting up to 60 kph are complicating firefighting efforts, and the Tour de France has shortened its final stage due to the emergency.
As of July 25-26, the number of evacuees across France and Spain has risen to over 300,000, with exhausted firefighters battling blazes fueled by high winds. At least one death has been confirmed in Spain, and the Tour de France final stage has been shortened to free up security personnel for firefighting efforts.
A new wildfire broke out in Castellon, Valencia, forcing 15,000 evacuations. As of July 26, France has evacuated about 220,000 people and Spain over 75,000 (with 30,000 ordered to shelter in place), while Bordeaux considered a total evacuation as fires advanced to within 15 kilometers of the city. French President Macron called a crisis cabinet meeting for Monday to address the escalating situation.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

Hollywood star George Clooney evacuated his French home due to a nearby fire. In France, authorities are using water cannons and international aid to control the situation. Cooler weather and rain are helping efforts, but conditions remain challenging.

news.body: Firefighters have contained a vast wildfire in southwestern France, allowing nearly 200,000 people to return home. The development comes after what may have been the country’s largest peacetime evacuation. However, renewed fires have forced thousands from their homes in other parts of France and Greece. In the Var region, a fire thought to be under control raced across 10 square kilometers in just six hours. Meanwhile, in Greece, gale-force winds have driven flames through the coastal area between Athens and Thebes, leading to evacuations. Rising temperatures and prolonged droughts are making Europe more vulnerable to such wildfires.
